cor-qf-mahalanobis.title: Mahalanobis forms
cor-qf-mahalanobis.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ).

  1. If Σ is positive definite, 𝛍𝛍(Y−μ)⊤Σ−1(Y−μ)∼χ2(n) and 𝛍𝛍Y⊤Σ−1Y∼χ2(n,μ⊤Σ−1μ).

  2. If G is a symmetric generalized inverse of Σ and 𝛍μ∈C(Σ), then 𝛍𝛍Y⊤GY∼χ2(rank(Σ),μ⊤Gμ).

cor-qf-mgf.title: Moment generating function
cor-qf-mgf.html: In the setting of @thm-qf-canonical, for |t|<1/(2maxj|λj|) (any t if all λj=0), 𝛍𝛍EetY⊤AY=etμ⊤Aμ∏j=1k(1−2λjt)−1/2exp⁡(2bj2t21−2λjt).

cor-qf-sample-variance.title: Sample mean and sample variance
cor-qf-sample-variance.html:
Let Y1,…,Yn (n≥2) be independent N(μ,σ2), with sample mean Y¯ and sample variance S2=(n−1)−1∑i(Yi−Y¯)2. Then

  1. Y¯ and S2 are independent, and Y¯∼N(μ,σ2/n);

  2. (n−1)S2/σ2∼χ2(n−1);

  3. for any μ0, T=n(Y¯−μ0)/S∼t(n−1,δ) with δ=n(μ−μ0)/σ. In particular T∼t(n−1) when μ=μ0.

def-qf-noncentral-chisq.title: Noncentral chi-squared
def-qf-noncentral-chisq.html: Let 𝛍Z∼Nr(μ,Ir). The distribution of Z⊤Z=∑iZi2 is the noncentral chi-squared distribution with r degrees of freedom and noncentrality 𝛍𝛍𝛍γ=μ⊤μ=‖μ‖2, written χ2(r,γ).

def-qf-noncentral-f.title: Noncentral F
def-qf-noncentral-f.title_html: Noncentral F
def-qf-noncentral-f.html: Let U∼χ2(r,γ) and V∼χ2(s) be independent, r,s≥1. The law of F=U/rV/s is the noncentral F distribution F(r,s,γ), with numerator and denominator degrees of freedom r and s and noncentrality γ. The central F(r,s)=F(r,s,0) has upper α point Fα(r,s).

def-qf-noncentral-t.title: Noncentral t
def-qf-noncentral-t.title_html: Noncentral t
def-qf-noncentral-t.html: Let X∼N(δ,1) and V∼χ2(s) be independent. The law of T=X/V/s is the noncentral t distribution t(s,δ), and t(s)=t(s,0).

eq-qf-canonical.html: 𝛍𝛍Y⊤AY=dμ⊤Aμ+∑j=1k(λjWj2+2bjWj),W∼Nk(0,Ik).

eq-qf-chisq-density.html: gr(x)=xr/2−1e−x/22r/2Γ(r/2),x>0,

eq-qf-cumulant-match.html: ∑j∈Jλjk(1+kνj2)=r+kγfor every k≥1.

eq-qf-mean.html: 𝛍𝛍E(Y⊤AY)=tr(AΣ)+μ⊤Aμ.

eq-qf-ncchisq-density.html: fr,γ(x)=∑k=0∞e−γ/2(γ/2)kk!gr+2k(x),x>0.

eq-qf-ncchisq-mgf.html: MU(t)=(1−2t)−r/2exp⁡(γt1−2t),t<12,

exm-qf-curvature.title: Detecting curvature
exm-qf-curvature.html:
Let x1,…,xn, n=15, be equally spaced on [0,1], and suppose Yi=1+0.5xi+β2xi2+εi with independent N(0,1) errors. To test for curvature, compare the straight line (X0=[1,x]) with the quadratic (X=[1,x,x2]). The F statistic has 1 and 12 degrees of freedom, and the 5% critical value is 4.747. For β2=8.0, the listing finds γ=6.873 and power 0.673 from the noncentral F, and the rejection rate in 100,000 simulated data sets is 0.674.

The noncentrality has a clear meaning. It is β22 times the squared length of the part of x2 orthogonal to 1 and x, divided by σ2. It grows roughly in proportion to n for a fixed design pattern. Keeping the same design on [0,1], the smallest n with power at least 0.8 is 21, where γ=8.97. Figure 4.4.1 places the example on the power curve and shows the loss of power when the same noncentrality is spread over more numerator degrees of freedom r. At γ=10 the power is 0.827, 0.606 and 0.421 for r=1,3,6.

exm-qf-drift.title: Two estimators of \sigma^2 under a drifting mean
exm-qf-drift.title_html: Two estimators of σ2 under a drifting mean
exm-qf-drift.html:
Let Y1,…,Yn be uncorrelated with common variance σ2, and consider S2=1n−1∑i=1n(Yi−Y¯)2,Q=12(n−1)∑i=1n−1(Yi+1−Yi)2, the sample variance and the mean square successive difference. In matrix form S2=Y⊤CY/(n−1) with C=I−n−111⊤, and Q=Y⊤D⊤DY/{2(n−1)}, where D is the (n−1)×n first-difference matrix with rows (…,−1,1,…). Both matrices annihilate 1, so both estimators ignore a constant mean. Since tr(C)=n−1 and tr(D⊤D)=tr(DD⊤)=2(n−1), @eq-qf-mean with Σ=σ2I shows that both are unbiased when the mean is constant.

Now let the mean drift linearly, μi=μ0+θi. Then 𝛍Cμ is the centred trend and 𝛍Dμ=θ1n−1, so E(S2)=σ2+θ2n(n+1)12,E(Q)=σ2+θ22. The bias of S2 grows quadratically with the length of the series, while that of Q does not grow at all. With n=20, σ=1 and θ=0.1, the means are 1.350 and 1.005. Differencing removes smooth trends, and this is why Q was proposed for series whose level may wander (von Neumann 1941). The price of robustness to drift is paid in variance, which we compute below.

exm-qf-drift-variance.html:
[@exm-qf-drift, continued]

With Σ=σ2I and a constant mean, @thm-qf-mean-var(b) gives Var(S2)=2σ4tr(C2)/(n−1)2=2σ4/(n−1). For Q, the matrix DD⊤ is tridiagonal with 2 on the diagonal and −1 beside it, so tr{(D⊤D)2}=tr{(DD⊤)2}=4(n−1)+2(n−2)=6n−8 and Var(Q)=2σ4(6n−8)4(n−1)2=σ4(3n−4)(n−1)2. The ratio Var(Q)/Var(S2)=(3n−4)/{2(n−1)} tends to 3/2. With n=20 the two variances are 0.1551 and 0.1053, a ratio of 1.474. So with no drift, Q needs about half as many observations again to match S2. Under the drift θ=0.1, the signal term 𝛍𝛍4μ⊤AΣAμ raises the variances to 0.1552 and 0.1789. Combining variance and bias, the root mean squared errors are 0.394 for Q and 0.549 for S2. The listing evaluates the formulas, and the script confirms all eight moments with 400,000 simulated series.

exm-qf-gls-centring.title: Correlated observations about a common level
exm-qf-gls-centring.title_html: Correlated observations about a common level
exm-qf-gls-centring.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) with Σ positive definite, and suppose we want to measure how far Y is from a common level m1. The generalized least squares level is m^=1⊤Σ−1Y/1⊤Σ−11, and the natural discrepancy is (Y−m^1)⊤Σ−1(Y−m^1)=Y⊤AY with A=Σ−1−Σ−111⊤Σ−11⊤Σ−11. A direct multiplication gives AΣA=A, and tr(AΣ)=n−1. By @thm-qf-chisq(b) the form is noncentral chi-squared with n−1 degrees of freedom and noncentrality 𝛍𝛍μ⊤Aμ, which is zero exactly when 𝛍μ is constant. The listing takes n=8, an autoregressive correlation Σ=(ρ|i−j|) with ρ=0.6, and a linear trend in the mean, for which γ=4.200. Figure 4.3.1(a) compares 200,000 simulated values with the χ2(7,4.200) density.

exm-qf-ncx-four.title: A noncentral chi-squared with four degrees of freedom
exm-qf-ncx-four.title_html: A noncentral chi-squared with four degrees of freedom
exm-qf-ncx-four.html: Take r=4 and γ=6. The Poisson(3) weights of the central densities g4,g6,g8,g10 in @eq-qf-ncchisq-density are 0.050, 0.149, 0.224 and 0.224, and the mean and variance are 10 and 32. The listing checks the mixture against a library implementation of the density. The script also squares normal vectors with a mean of length 6 in an arbitrary direction, and their average squared length is 10.002. A test that rejects when a χ2(4) statistic exceeds its upper 5% point 9.488 rejects with probability 0.470 when the statistic is in fact χ2(4,6). Figure 4.1.1 shows how the density moves right and spreads out as γ grows.

exm-qf-oneway-cochran.title: The one-way layout
exm-qf-oneway-cochran.html:
Let observations fall into g groups of sizes n1,…,ng, with Yℓj independent N(μℓ,σ2). Let M replace each observation by its group mean, and P1=n−111⊤ by the grand mean. Then I=P1+(M−P1)+(I−M) splits ‖Y‖2 into nY¯2, the between-group sum of squares ∑ℓnℓ(Y¯ℓ−Y¯)2 and the within-group sum of squares ∑ℓ,j(Yℓj−Y¯ℓ)2. The three matrices are symmetric with ranks 1, g−1 and n−g, which add to n. Cochran’s theorem needs nothing more. The three sums of squares, divided by σ2, are independent noncentral chi-squared variables. Their noncentralities are nμ¯2/σ2, ∑ℓnℓ(μℓ−μ¯)2/σ2 with μ¯=∑ℓnℓμℓ/n, and 0. The last is zero because 𝛍𝛍Mμ=μ. The ratio of the between and within mean squares is F(g−1,n−g,γ) by @thm-qf-nested-f, and it is central iff all group means are equal.

The script uses g=3 groups of sizes 3,5,4, means 2,3,1.5, and σ=1, and draws 200,000 data sets. Table 4.5.1 compares the theoretical means ri+γi and variances 2ri+4γi with the simulated ones. The largest absolute correlation between the three sums of squares is 0.0013. As a check that goes beyond correlation, the proportion of data sets in which both the between and the within sums of squares exceed their medians is 0.2497, against 0.25 for independent variables.

exr-qf-best-quadratic.title: C1
exr-qf-best-quadratic.html: Let Y∼Nn(μ1,σ2I) with μ and σ2 unknown. Among symmetric A with E(Y⊤AY)=σ2 for all μ and σ2, show that A=C/(n−1), which gives S2, uniquely minimizes Var(Y⊤AY) at every parameter value. (Compare @exr-rv-best-quadratic, where the mean is known to be zero.)

exr-qf-beta.title: B4
exr-qf-beta.html: Let U∼χ2(a) and V∼χ2(b) be independent. Show that B=U/(U+V) has the Beta(a/2,b/2) distribution and is independent of U+V, and that F=(U/a)/(V/b)=(b/a)B/(1−B). Deduce the null distribution of R2 asked for in Chapter 6.

exr-qf-chisq-two.title: A1
exr-qf-chisq-two.html: Show that χ2(2) is the exponential distribution with mean 2. Use @thm-qf-ncchisq(d) to show that Pr{χ2(2,γ)>x}=∑k≥0e−γ/2(γ/2)kk!e−x/2∑j=0k(x/2)jj!.

exr-qf-cochran-fails.title: A1
exr-qf-cochran-fails.html: Let A1=diag(2,0) and A2=diag(−1,1), so that A1+A2=I2. Which hypotheses of @thm-qf-cochran fail, and what are the laws of the two forms when Y∼N2(0,I)?

exr-qf-cumulants.title: B1
exr-qf-cumulants.html: Show that the kth cumulant of χ2(r,γ) is 2k−1(k−1)!(r+kγ). Deduce that its skewness tends to zero like 3/γ as γ→∞ with r fixed.

exr-qf-drift-independence.title: A1
exr-qf-drift-independence.html: In @exm-qf-drift let Y∼Nn(μ1,σ2I) with n≥3. Use @thm-qf-mean-var(d) to show that Cov(S2,Q)=Var(S2), and deduce that S2 and Q are dependent with correlation {2(n−1)/(3n−4)}1/2. Which linear forms a⊤Y are independent of Q for every mean vector 𝛍μ∈Rn?

exr-qf-equicorrelated.title: B1
exr-qf-equicorrelated.html: Let Y∼Nn(μ1,σ2{(1−ρ)I+ρ11⊤}) with −1/(n−1)<ρ<1, and let Y¯ and S2 be the sample mean and variance. Show that (n−1)S2/{σ2(1−ρ)}∼χ2(n−1) and that S2 is independent of Y¯. Deduce that n(Y¯−μ)/S has the law of {(1+(n−1)ρ)/(1−ρ)}1/2 times a t(n−1) variable, and describe what a positive ρ does to the coverage of the usual 95% t interval for μ.

exr-qf-f-limit.title: B4
exr-qf-f-limit.html: Show that Fα(r,s)→χα2(r)/r as s→∞, where χα2(r) is the upper α point of χ2(r), and that the power Pr{F(r,s,γ)>Fα(r,s)} tends to Pr{χ2(r,γ)>χα2(r)}, the power of the test that knows σ2.

exr-qf-ginverse-form.title: B3
exr-qf-ginverse-form.html: In @cor-qf-mahalanobis(b), show that Y⊤GY takes the same value for every generalized inverse G of Σ, with probability one. Hint: @thm-rv-cov-nnd.

exr-qf-hogg-craig.title: C1
exr-qf-hogg-craig.html: Let Y∼Nn(0,I), and Q=Q1+Q2 with Q=Y⊤AY∼χ2(r), Q1=Y⊤A1Y∼χ2(r1) and Q2=Y⊤A2Y for a nonnegative definite A2. Show that Q1 and Q2 are independent and Q2∼χ2(r−r1).

exr-qf-kurtosis.title: B2
exr-qf-kurtosis.html: Let Y1,…,Yn be independent with mean 0, variance σ2 and EYi4=μ4. By @exr-rv-cov-quadforms, for symmetric A and B, Cov(Y⊤AY,Y⊤BY)=(μ4−3σ4)∑iaiibii+2σ4tr(AB). Show that in a one-way layout with g≥2 groups, not all of size one, the between-group and within-group sums of squares are correlated unless μ4=3σ4. Which sign does the correlation have for heavy-tailed errors?

exr-qf-mgf-det.title: B4
exr-qf-mgf-det.html: Let Y∼Nn(0,Σ). Use @cor-qf-mgf and @prp-mat-eigen-basic(d) to show that EetY⊤AY=det(In−2tAΣ)−1/2 for |t| small.

exr-qf-mlr.title: B5
exr-qf-mlr.html: Show that fr,γ(x)/gr(x) is strictly increasing in x>0 for every γ>0. Conclude that among tests based on one observation U∼χ2(r,γ) of γ=0 against a fixed γ>0, rejecting for large U is most powerful.

exr-qf-necessity-singular.title: C1
exr-qf-necessity-singular.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) with Σ possibly singular, and suppose Y⊤AY∼χ2(r,γ) with r≥1. Show that ΣAΣAΣ=ΣAΣ. Hint: in @cor-qf-mgf, compare the coefficients of tk for k≥3 with those of @eq-qf-ncchisq-mgf, and adapt the argument of @thm-qf-chisq-identity.

exr-qf-normal-limit.title: B3
exr-qf-normal-limit.html: Let Uγ∼χ2(r,γ) with r fixed. Show that (Uγ−r−γ)/2r+4γ converges in distribution to N(0,1) as γ→∞. Hint: Uγ has the law of (W1+γ)2+W22+⋯+Wr2 with W1,…,Wr independent standard normal.

exr-qf-one-df-density.title: B2
exr-qf-one-df-density.html: Show that χ2(1,γ) has density (2πx)−1/2e−(x+γ)/2cosh⁡γx for x>0. Verify that expanding cosh in a power series reproduces @eq-qf-ncchisq-density. Hint: Γ(k+12)=π(2k)!/(4kk!).

exr-qf-regression-t.title: B3
exr-qf-regression-t.html: Let 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2I) with X of full column rank p<n, let 𝛃β^=(X⊤X)−1X⊤Y, M=X(X⊤X)−1X⊤ and s2=‖(I−M)Y‖2/(n−p). With vjj the jth diagonal entry of (X⊤X)−1, show that (β^j−b)/(svjj)∼t(n−p,(βj−b)/(σvjj)).

exr-qf-sample-cov-var.title: B1
exr-qf-sample-cov-var.html: Let (Ui,Wi), i=1,…,n, be independent copies of a bivariate normal pair with variances σU2, σW2 and covariance σUW, and let sUW=(n−1)−1∑i(Ui−U¯)(Wi−W¯). Write sUW=Y⊤AY for the stacked vector Y=(U⊤,W⊤)⊤ and a symmetric 2n×2n matrix A, and use @thm-qf-mean-var to show that Var(sUW)=(σU2σW2+σUW2)/(n−1). Check the answer against Var(S2) when U=W.

exr-qf-satterthwaite.title: B4
exr-qf-satterthwaite.html: Let Y∼Nn(0,Σ) with Σ positive definite, and let A≠0 be nonnegative definite. Show that the two-moment approximation aχ2(ν) to Y⊤AY has ν={tr(AΣ)}2/tr{(AΣ)2}, and that ν≤rank(A), with equality iff all nonzero eigenvalues of AΣ are equal.

exr-qf-sequential.title: B2
exr-qf-sequential.html: Let P1,…,Pm be symmetric idempotent with C(P1)⊂C(P2)⊂⋯⊂C(Pm), and put P0=0, Pm+1=I. Show that the matrices Pi−Pi−1, i=1,…,m+1, satisfy the conditions of @thm-qf-cochran, so that the sequential sums of squares ‖(Pi−Pi−1)Y‖2 are independent noncentral chi-squared variables when 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,σ2I).

exr-qf-singular.title: B2
exr-qf-singular.html: Let Σ=diag(1,0), 𝛍μ=(0,1)⊤, A=I2 and 𝛍Y∼N2(μ,Σ). Show that AΣ is idempotent but Y⊤AY is not chi-squared. Which of the conditions of @thm-qf-chisq(c) fail? What changes if 𝛍μ=(m,0)⊤? Repeat the first part with A=(1110), where the shift enters through a linear term.

exr-qf-singular-independence.title: B2
exr-qf-singular-independence.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) and let A,B be nonnegative definite with ΣAΣBΣ=0. Show that AΣB=0, so that Y⊤AY and Y⊤BY are independent. Show by an example that the implication can fail when A is not nonnegative definite.

exr-qf-sse-bias.title: B3
exr-qf-sse-bias.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,σ2I), and let M be symmetric idempotent of rank r with 𝛍𝛍Mμ≠μ, as when a regression model omits a needed regressor. Show that 𝛍‖(I−M)Y‖2/σ2∼χ2(n−r,‖(I−M)μ‖2/σ2), and find the bias of ‖(I−M)Y‖2/(n−r) as an estimator of σ2. In the setting of @thm-qf-nested-f without the assumption 𝛍𝛍Pμ=μ, which parts of the conclusion survive?

exr-qf-symmetrize.title: A1
exr-qf-symmetrize.html: Let Y∼N2(0,I) and A=(0100). Compute Var(Y⊤AY) directly, and compare with 2tr(A2) and with 2tr(As2), where As=12(A+A⊤).

exr-qf-t-square.title: A2
exr-qf-t-square.html: Show that T∼t(s,δ) implies T2∼F(1,s,δ2). Deduce that the power of the two-sided level-α t test depends on δ only through |δ| and increases with it. Show directly, by conditioning on the denominator, that the power of the one-sided test that rejects for T>c increases with δ.

exr-qf-two-sample.title: A2
exr-qf-two-sample.html: Two independent samples of sizes m and k come from N(μ1,σ2) and N(μ2,σ2). Write the pooled within-sample sum of squares as ‖(I−M)Y‖2 for a suitable projection, and show that the two-sample t statistic has the t(m+k−2,(μ1−μ2)/(σ1/m+1/k)) distribution.

exr-qf-twoway.title: B1
exr-qf-twoway.html: A two-way layout has one observation Yij for each of a rows and b columns. Write ‖Y‖2 as the sum of the grand-mean, row, column and residual sums of squares, identify the four matrices, and use @thm-qf-cochran to show that under Yij∼N(μ+αi+βj,σ2) independently the four sums of squares are independent, with degrees of freedom 1, a−1, b−1 and (a−1)(b−1).

exr-qf-uncorrelated-dependent.title: B1
exr-qf-uncorrelated-dependent.html: Let Y∼N2(0,I). Show that Y12−Y22 and 2Y1Y2 are uncorrelated but not independent. Why does @prp-qf-craig-nnd not apply?

exr-qf-which-idempotent.title: A1
exr-qf-which-idempotent.html: Let Y∼Nn(0,I) with n≥2, and A=αI+β11⊤. Find all (α,β) for which Y⊤AY has a chi-squared distribution, and identify each form.

lem-qf-shifted-square.html: Let W∼N(0,1) and ν∈R. For t<1/2, E[et(W+ν)2]=(1−2t)−1/2exp⁡(ν2t1−2t).

prp-qf-craig-nnd.title: Necessity for nonnegative definite forms
prp-qf-craig-nnd.html: Let Y∼Nn(0,I) and let A,B be nonnegative definite. If Y⊤AY and Y⊤BY are independent, then AB=0.

prp-qf-ncchisq-monotone.title: Monotonicity in the noncentrality
prp-qf-ncchisq-monotone.html: For fixed r≥1 and x>0, the tail probability γ↦Pr{χ2(r,γ)>x} is continuous and strictly increasing on [0,∞), and tends to 1 as γ→∞.

thm-qf-canonical.title: Canonical form of a normal quadratic form
thm-qf-canonical.title_html: Canonical form of a normal quadratic form
thm-qf-canonical.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) and let A be symmetric. Write Σ=LL⊤ with L of size n×k, and take a spectral decomposition L⊤AL=QΛQ⊤ with Λ=diag(λ1,…,λk). Put 𝛍b=Q⊤L⊤Aμ. Then 𝛍𝛍Y⊤AY=dμ⊤Aμ+∑j=1k(λjWj2+2bjWj),W∼Nk(0,Ik).{#eq-qf-canonical}

For λj≠0 the jth term equals λj(Wj+bj/λj)2−bj2/λj. The nonzero λj are the nonzero eigenvalues of AΣ.

thm-qf-chisq.title: When a quadratic form is chi-squared
thm-qf-chisq.title_html: When a quadratic form is chi-squared
thm-qf-chisq.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) and let A be symmetric.

  1. (Projections.) If Σ=σ2I with σ>0 and P is symmetric and idempotent, then 𝛍‖PY‖2σ2=Y⊤PYσ2∼χ2(rank(P),‖Pμ‖2σ2).

  2. (Positive definite Σ.) If Σ is positive definite, then Y⊤AY has a χ2(r,γ) distribution for some r≥1 and γ≥0 iff AΣ is idempotent and A≠0. In that case r=rank(A)=tr(AΣ) and 𝛍𝛍γ=μ⊤Aμ.

  3. (Any Σ.) If 𝛍𝛍𝛍𝛍𝛍𝛍(i) ΣAΣAΣ=ΣAΣ,(ii) ΣAΣAμ=ΣAμ,(iii) μ⊤AΣAμ=μ⊤Aμ, then 𝛍𝛍Y⊤AY∼χ2(tr(AΣ),μ⊤Aμ). The three conditions hold in particular when AΣA=A, and when AΣ is idempotent and 𝛍μ∈C(Σ).

thm-qf-chisq-identity.title: Chi-squared forms in a spherical normal vector
thm-qf-chisq-identity.title_html: Chi-squared forms in a spherical normal vector
thm-qf-chisq-identity.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,In), let A be symmetric, and let r≥1 be an integer and γ≥0. Then Y⊤AY∼χ2(r,γ) if and only if A is idempotent with rank(A)=r and 𝛍𝛍γ=μ⊤Aμ.

thm-qf-cochran.title: Cochran
thm-qf-cochran.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,σ2I), and let A1,…,Ak be symmetric with ranks r1,…,rk, whose sum A=∑iAi is idempotent of rank r (for example A=I, r=n). The following are equivalent:

  1. the forms Y⊤AiY/σ2 are mutually independent, and 𝛍𝛍Y⊤AiY/σ2∼χ2(ri,μ⊤Aiμ/σ2) for each i;

  2. r1+⋯+rk=r;

  3. each Ai is idempotent;

  4. AiAj=0 for all i≠j.

thm-qf-cochran-algebra.title: Cochran, algebraic form
thm-qf-cochran-algebra.html:
Let A1,…,Ak be symmetric n×n matrices and A=∑iAi. Consider

  1. each Ai is idempotent;

  2. AiAj=0 for all i≠j;

  3. A is idempotent;

  4. rank(A)=∑irank(Ai).

Then any two of (a), (b), (c) imply all four, and (c) together with (d) implies all four.

thm-qf-f-power.title: Power of the F test increases with \gamma
thm-qf-f-power.title_html: Power of the F test increases with γ
thm-qf-f-power.html: For fixed r,s≥1 and c>0, β(γ)=Pr{F(r,s,γ)>c} is continuous and strictly increasing in γ≥0, and β(γ)→1 as γ→∞. In particular, the level-α test that rejects when F>Fα(r,s) has power greater than α at every γ>0.

thm-qf-indep-linear.title: Linear and quadratic forms
thm-qf-indep-linear.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ), let B be m×n and A symmetric n×n. If BΣA=0, then BY and Y⊤AY are independent. Conversely, if BY and Y⊤AY are independent for every 𝛍μ∈Rn, with Σ fixed, then BΣA=0.

thm-qf-indep-quadratic.title: Two quadratic forms
thm-qf-indep-quadratic.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) and let A,B be symmetric. If AΣB=0, equivalently BΣA=0, then Y⊤AY and Y⊤BY are independent.

thm-qf-mean-var.title: Moments of normal quadratic forms
thm-qf-mean-var.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ), let A and B be symmetric n×n matrices, and let K be an m×n matrix. Then

  1. 𝛍𝛍E(Y⊤AY)=tr(AΣ)+μ⊤Aμ;

  2. 𝛍𝛍Var(Y⊤AY)=2tr{(AΣ)2}+4μ⊤AΣAμ;

  3. 𝛍Cov(KY,Y⊤AY)=2KΣAμ;

  4. 𝛍𝛍Cov(Y⊤AY,Y⊤BY)=2tr(AΣBΣ)+4μ⊤AΣBμ.

thm-qf-ncchisq.title: Properties of the noncentral chi-squared
thm-qf-ncchisq.html:
Let U∼χ2(r,γ).

  1. The moment generating function is MU(t)=(1−2t)−r/2exp⁡(γt1−2t),t<12,{#eq-qf-ncchisq-mgf}

    so the law depends on 𝛍μ only through γ, and χ2(r,0)=χ2(r).

  2. E(U)=r+γ and Var(U)=2r+4γ.

  3. If U1,…,Uk are independent with Ui∼χ2(ri,γi), then ∑iUi∼χ2(∑iri,∑iγi).

  4. (Poisson mixture.) Let K∼Poisson(γ/2) and, given K=k, let V∼χ2(r+2k). Then V∼χ2(r,γ). Consequently U has density fr,γ(x)=∑k=0∞e−γ/2(γ/2)kk!gr+2k(x),x>0.{#eq-qf-ncchisq-density}

thm-qf-nested-f.title: F statistic for nested subspaces
thm-qf-nested-f.title_html: F statistic for nested subspaces
thm-qf-nested-f.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,σ2I), and let P0 and P be symmetric idempotent matrices of ranks r0<r<n with PP0=P0. Suppose that 𝛍𝛍Pμ=μ. Then 𝛍F=Y⊤(P−P0)Y/(r−r0)Y⊤(I−P)Y/(n−r)∼F(r−r0,n−r,‖(P−P0)μ‖2σ2), and the noncentrality is zero iff 𝛍𝛍P0μ=μ.

thm-qf-orthogonal-projections.title: Independent projections
thm-qf-orthogonal-projections.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,σ2I), and let P1,…,Pk be symmetric idempotent matrices with PiPj=0 for i≠j, and ranks r1,…,rk. Then P1Y,…,PkY are mutually independent normal vectors, 𝛍PiY∼Nn(Piμ,σ2Pi), and the sums of squares 𝛍‖PiY‖2σ2∼χ2(ri,‖Piμ‖2σ2),i=1,…,k, are mutually independent.
